subject.title: Session files not being cleaned up (disk bloat)

question: What durable lifecycle should OpenClaw enforce for session archive artifacts beyond the deleted/reset cleanup already covered by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/97103?
rationale: Current code intentionally preserves `.bak.*` archives in normal retention while other open reports argue both for more cleanup and for never deleting archived transcripts, so automation should not pick the data-retention policy.

options.title: Narrow cleanup plus explicit archive policy
options.body: Review or replace the deleted/reset reporting PR first, then specify a single retention policy for `.bak.*`, orphan transcripts/checkpoints, and proactive sweeps before queuing another fix.

options.title: Keep cleanup operator-driven
options.body: Keep startup reads cheap and require `openclaw sessions cleanup --enforce` or a future explicit command for physical artifact cleanup.

options.title: Adopt proactive cleanup
options.body: Make gateway startup or a timer run a bounded artifact sweep, accepting the need for stronger upgrade and data-retention proof.

recommendation.title: Narrow cleanup plus explicit archive policy
recommendation.body: Review or replace the deleted/reset reporting PR first, then specify a single retention policy for `.bak.*`, orphan transcripts/checkpoints, and proactive sweeps before queuing another fix.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main history and adjacent cleanup/source-seam changes make this the strongest available routing signal for the product decision.
